open.title: The Riemann hypothesis
open.summary: Whether every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2. Open since 1859. A proof would sharpen what is known about the distribution of prime numbers; a great deal of published number theory is currently stated conditionally on it holding.

open.title: P versus NP
open.summary: Whether every problem whose solution can be verified quickly can also be solved quickly. Formalised in 1971. The answer determines whether large parts of cryptography rest on genuine hardness or on an unproven assumption.

open.title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
open.summary: Whether smooth solutions to the Navier–Stokes equations always exist in three dimensions, or whether they can blow up in finite time. The equations are used daily in engineering; nobody has shown they always behave.

open.title: The hard problem of consciousness
open.summary: Why physical processing in a brain is accompanied by subjective experience at all. Distinguished by Chalmers from the 'easy' problems of explaining discrimination, integration and report, which are hard but not of this kind. It is contested whether this is a scientific question, which is itself part of the problem.

sources.label: Chalmers, Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness (1995)

open.title: What dark matter is made of
open.summary: Roughly a quarter of the mass-energy of the universe is inferred from gravitational effects but has never been directly detected. Decades of increasingly sensitive direct-detection experiments have returned null results, ruling out much of the parameter space once considered most likely.

sources.label: Particle Data Group — Dark Matter review

blocked.title: Direct imaging of an exoplanet's surface
blocked.summary: Resolving surface features on a planet around another star is well-posed and uncontroversially desirable. It is blocked by angular resolution: separating surface detail at interstellar distance needs apertures or interferometric baselines far beyond anything built or funded. No idea is missing; the instrument is.

blocked.title: A direct sample of the Earth's lower mantle
blocked.summary: Everything known about the lower mantle is inferred from seismology, xenoliths and high-pressure experiments. The deepest borehole ever drilled, the Kola Superdeep, reached about 12 km — still within the crust. Drilling technology, not theory, is the constraint.

sources.label: International Ocean Discovery Program — Mohole to Mantle

blocked.title: Randomised trials of lifetime dietary exposure in humans
blocked.summary: Most claims about long-term diet rest on observational cohorts with well-known confounding. The trial that would settle them — randomising people to decades of controlled intake — cannot ethically be run, and compliance would not survive it. The uncertainty is structural, not a gap in anyone's ideas.

sources.label: Ioannidis, The Challenge of Reforming Nutritional Epidemiology (JAMA 2018)

blocked.title: Biological effects of multi-generational spaceflight
blocked.summary: Whether humans can reproduce and develop normally across generations in partial gravity and elevated radiation. Answering it requires observations spanning generations in an environment that does not yet exist. Rodent analogues answer a related but different question.

sources.label: NASA Human Research Program — evidence reports

blocked.title: Whether the proton decays
blocked.summary: Grand unified theories predict proton decay; experiments have pushed the lower bound on the lifetime past 10^34 years. Testing further means instrumenting ever more protons for ever longer, since no single proton can be watched for its lifetime. Each order of magnitude costs a detector generation.

blind-spots.title: Craft, practitioner and indigenous knowledge
blind-spots.summary: OpenAlex indexes academic publishing. Knowledge held by practitioners and transmitted by apprenticeship, demonstration or oral tradition is not merely under-represented here — it is absent, because it was never a paper. Nothing in this map can register a gap in it, including the gap that it is missing.

blind-spots.title: Humanities citations are only partly linked
blind-spots.summary: Reference linkage in OpenAlex runs near 95% for STEM but around 70% for arts and humanities, where monographs and non-English venues carry much of the scholarship. Every co-occurrence and citation measure in this project is correspondingly weaker there, and a computed gap in the humanities means less than the same number in molecular biology.

sources.label: Reference coverage of OpenAlex compared to Web of Science and Scopus
An analysis of the suitability of OpenAlex for bibliometric analyses

blind-spots.title: Literature before about 1970 thins out sharply
blind-spots.summary: Measured on 2026-07-27: OpenAlex holds roughly 1.38M works published in 1980, 1.05M in 1970, but only 305K in 1950 — about a fifth of the 1980 density. Historical analyses become progressively less trustworthy the further back they reach, and an apparent gap in older literature may simply be an unindexed one.

blind-spots.title: Historical slices use today's ontology, not the period's
blind-spots.summary: OpenAlex assigns topics with a model trained on the modern corpus and applies it retroactively. Filtering to works published before 1986 therefore does not reconstruct the literature as it was organised in 1986 — it projects the 2026 classification backwards onto it. Any claim about what was knowable at a past date inherits this distortion.

blind-spots.title: The computed gap layer failed its own validation
blind-spots.summary: The Swanson-style metric this project was built around does not reproduce the canonical result it was tested against. On pre-1986 data the fish-oil / Raynaud's pair ranks at top 30.8% of scored pairs against a pre-registered bar of top 5%. Two metric designs failed the same way: 'structurally close but rarely co-occurring' is dominated by adjacent clinical specialties that split papers between them rather than by holes in knowledge. No computed gaps are published as discoveries.

blind-spots.title: Some topics are dumping grounds for unclassifiable work
blind-spots.summary: OpenAlex assigns a topic to every work, so works with thin metadata land wherever the classifier defaults. 'Military Technology and Strategies' holds 22.3M works — 7% of the entire corpus — and 'Diverse Scientific and Economic Studies' holds 5.1M. These are artifacts of classification, not fields of that size, and any measure averaged over them is meaningless.
